clue.text: Illusion of precious metal buried in soil

indicators.note: buried in says the metal is sunk inside the word for soil

parts.note: mire is boggy ground, wet soil
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, a precious metal

explanation.surface: A prospector's dream of gold or silver in the ground turns out to be a delusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, such as water seen shimmering in a desert that is not there.

clue.text: Intended to go over two forms for setter in the interim

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means sitting above the following pieces

parts.note: intended means meant, as in meant to do it
the setter refers to themself as I
the setter's object form, me

explanation.surface: A setter planned to revise two drafts while waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Meantime is used adverbially to mean meanwhile, during the period between two events.

clue.text: Seclusion once found in it-terra nova?

indicators.note: nova is Latin for new, so the letters of it-terra are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hermit's retreat was supposedly discovered in some new land, a terra nova.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the definition as archaic: retrait is an obsolete word for a retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrait is an old word for a retreat or withdrawal, a place or state of seclusion.

clue.text: A dial ultimately raised above base of spirit compass

indicators.note: in a down clue above means the first part sits over the next
in a down clue raised means lifted to the top, so the final letter of the a-dial pair climbs to the front

parts.note: dial is slang for face, as is mug

indicators.note: base of in a down clue means the bottom, final letter of spirit

explanation.surface: A gauge on a spirit compass is lifted at last above its base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately raised' lifts G, the last letter of A MUG, to the top of the down light: GAMU. 'base of' takes T, the bottom of 'spirit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass here means range or scope, and a gamut is the full range of something.

clue.text: Shell-disposal specialist that clears a path for soldiers

definitions.text: Shell-disposal specialist that clears a path for soldiers

parts.words: Shell-disposal specialist that clears a path for soldiers
parts.note: reads like an army bomb-disposal expert, but the shell is a boiled egg's and the soldiers are toast strips dipped in the yolk

explanation.surface: An army sapper who clears unexploded shells so troops can advance.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are thin strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg; the shell is the eggshell, opened with the utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon is used to crack and scoop a boiled egg, opening the way for toast strips.

clue.text: Almost maimed a character

indicators.note: almost means the word for maimed is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: gammy is British slang for lame or injured, as in a gammy leg

explanation.surface: Someone was nearly crippled by a certain person.
explanation.walkthrough: GAMMY is informal British for injured or lame; 'Almost' drops its Y to leave GAMM.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Unexpected report from out of the blue?

definitions.text: Unexpected report from out of the blue?

parts.words: Unexpected report from out of the blue
parts.note: out of the blue usually means suddenly, but here it is literally from the sky, and a report is a loud bang

explanation.surface: Some surprising news arrives without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A supersonic aircraft overhead produces a sudden explosive bang heard on the ground.

clue.text: The best man's put on a stone

indicators.note: put on is read as placed onto, here set within, the gemstone

parts.note: an opal is a gemstone
Tim is a man's name, a typical crossword 'man'

explanation.surface: The best man at a wedding is given a stone to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal means most favourable or ideal, the finest possible.

clue.text: Model marries a girl

parts.note: a norm is a standard or model to follow

explanation.surface: A fashion model weds a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female first name, and a girl in crosswords is often any woman's name.

clue.text: Volunteers beating a retreat to attract assault

indicators.note: beating a retreat means going backwards, so the letters for volunteers are written in reverse

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
to tempt is to lure or attract

explanation.surface: Soldiers fall back in order to draw the enemy into an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army (TA) was Britain's part-time volunteer reserve; reversed it gives AT.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt can mean an attack, as in an attempt on someone's life.

clue.text: Tailless bird sits On dish on alternate days

indicators.note: in a down clue sitting on means placed above the next piece
tailless means the bird's word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
a tian is a Provencal baked vegetable dish, named after its earthenware pot

explanation.surface: A bird missing its tail perches on a plate every other day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' cuts TERN to TER. A tian is a French earthenware dish and what is baked in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tertian describes a fever recurring every second day, as in malaria.

clue.text: Watch VDU

definitions.meaning: to observe or keep under surveillance
a visual display unit, a computer screen

explanation.definitionFit: To keep an eye on is to observe; and a computer screen is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Foreign restaurant about to display extreme cunning

indicators.note: about says the whole string of pieces is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to air is to display or show off
OTT, over the top, means extreme
art can mean cunning or craftiness

explanation.surface: A foreign eatery is about to show off its great craftiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole run of three pieces round, so each is read backwards and their order reverses; 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an Italian eating house, a restaurant of foreign origin to English speakers.

clue.text: One or two of us turn up to introduce speech

definitions.text: One or two of us turn up to introduce speech

parts.words: One or two of us turn up to introduce speech
parts.note: a punctuation mark speaks: one of them often precedes a quotation, and two of them turned upside down become inverted quotation marks

explanation.surface: A couple of us show up to give a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Quotation marks are called 'inverted commas' in Britain, so a pair of these marks turned up opens speech.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark can introduce direct speech, and two of them inverted are quotation marks.

clue.text: Books contributing to assembled composition

indicators.note: contributing to says the books are put into the word for assembled

parts.note: met means gathered or assembled
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Books were donated to a gathered collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral piece, a musical composition usually sacred.

clue.text: Close call: one getting put away around noon

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it

indicators.note: around says the pieces for one and put away go round the abbreviation for noon

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
to put food away is to eat it, ate

explanation.surface: A narrow escape: someone nearly jailed at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to end or finish something, bring it to a close.

clue.text: Diamonds ready? That'll take the heat off

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
the ready and lolly are both British slang for cash

explanation.surface: A jewel thief asks if the money is ready, saying that will ease the police pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' and 'lolly' are British slang for money; an ice lolly is a frozen treat on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen flavoured treat on a stick cools you down on a hot day.

clue.text: Dish of cola stirred in an unusual sense

indicators.note: in places the stirred letters inside the abbreviation for the unusual sense

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is an unusual sixth sense

indicators.note: stirred means the letters of cola are mixed up

explanation.surface: A drink of cola mixed with an odd sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' makes CALO from COLA, which goes 'in' ESP.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin slice of meat, fried as a dish; escalop is a variant spelling.

clue.text: Damp-course company leaving damaged hatches

indicators.note: damaged signals the remaining letters of the fodder are rearranged

explanation.surface: A building firm walks away from a broken damp-proof course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes CO out of DAMPCOURSE, and 'damaged' rearranges the rest, DAMPURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream up a plot is to hatch it, inventing a scheme.

clue.text: See dry bishop admitted due to a particular form of the shakes?

definitions.text: due to a particular form of the shakes?

parts.note: v is short for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: admitted means the bishop is let inside the word for dry

parts.note: dry humour is ironic
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop with a dry wit is treated for tremors.
explanation.walkthrough: V (vide) is the reference abbreviation for 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibronic describes combined vibrational and electronic states of molecules, a technical kind of shaking.

clue.text: To some extent, find or secure sanction

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Somewhat, discovering or guaranteeing approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Indorse is a variant spelling of endorse, to approve or ratify.

clue.text: I declare "I'm back dear!" regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of I'm back dear

explanation.surface: A spouse calls out 'I'm home, darling!' as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the maker is the declarer, the player who names the trump suit and plays the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, the player who wins the auction and names trumps is the declarer, also called the maker.

clue.text: King remains on edge, climbing somewhere in Asia

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ash is what remains after burning

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word for edge is read upwards

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A monarch's remains lie at a mountain edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashmir is a region in the north of the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Note senior copper reported bones

indicators.note: reported means the words are said aloud and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: ray is a note in sol-fa, and DI, detective inspector, is a senior police officer

explanation.surface: A senior policeman notes that skeletal remains have been found.
explanation.walkthrough: RAY plus DI, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone, so this plural form names several of them.

clue.text: Revolutionary emblem alternately captured by both sides

indicators.note: captured by means the picked letters are held between right and left

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left, the two sides

indicators.note: alternately takes every other letter of emblem

explanation.surface: A revolutionary badge is seized in turn by both factions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternately' picks E, B, E from EMBLEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel rises against authority, a revolutionary insurgent.

clue.text: Slowly ease off, leaving behind southern part of ocean

indicators.note: off signals the letters are rearranged once a letter is removed

explanation.surface: Gradually throttle back, leaving the south seas behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving behind' drops one S from SLOWLY EASE and 'off' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea lies between China and Korea, an arm of the Pacific.

clue.text: Talk idly with spirit and get work down under.

parts.note: to yak is to chatter idly
ka is the Egyptian word for the spirit or soul

explanation.surface: Gossip with some booze and get a job in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Yakka is Australian slang for hard work, as in hard yakka.

clue.text: Pontificate, implicitly going nowhere?

parts.note: nowhere suggests nothing, the letter O for zero
going as in the going rate, so going means rate

explanation.surface: To lecture pompously is, it seems, to get nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as O-RATE, a rate of nought, speed going nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak pompously at length, to sound off.

clue.text: Arrives to stop champion? Boo!

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, here sitting within the word for champion

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it
arr. is the abbreviation for arrives in timetables

explanation.surface: Someone turns up to stop the champion and is jeered.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to jeer or heckle, especially at sport.

clue.text: As lamps are heating up to release hot gases

indicators.note: heating up suggests the letters of as lamps are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: Lamps warming up give off hot gases.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is ionised gas at very high temperature, a fourth state of matter.

clue.text: Subject title rejected by one blocking support

indicators.note: blocking means the numeral for one sits inside the word for support

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: rejected means the word for title is turned back

parts.note: a name is a title

explanation.surface: A subject refuses a title offered by someone who is blocking his advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal vassal owed allegiance to a lord, so he was a lord's subject.

clue.text: Lose it three times, the last two as the first?

indicators.text: the last two as the first
indicators.note: the last two letters of the word for three times are moved to the front

parts.note: triple means three times

explanation.surface: Losing your temper over and over, with the last two going first.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way to anger or emotion without restraint, to explode.
